statement: In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles.
heath_proof: Let ABC be a triangle, and let one side of it BC be produced to D; I say that the exterior angle ACD is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles CBA, BAC. Let AC be bisected at E [I. 10], and let BE be joined and producedin a straight line to F; let EF be made equal to BE [I. 3], let FC be joined [Post. 1], and let AC be drawn through to G [Post. 2]. Then, since AE is equal to EC,and BE to EF, the two sides AE, EB are equal to the two sides CE, EF respectively; and the angle AEB is equal to the angle FEC, for they are vertical angles. [I. 15]Therefore the base AB is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABE is equal to the triangle CFE, and the remaining angles are equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]therefore the angle BAE is equal to the angle ECF. But the angle ECD is greater than the angle ECF; [C. N. 5]therefore the angle ACD is greater than the angle BAE. Similarly also, if BC be bisected, the angle BCG, that is, the angle ACD [I. 15], can be proved greater than the angle ABC as well.
ai_proof_text:
1.16
**Statement:** In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles.

**Step 1.** Let ABC be any triangle, and let one of its sides, BC, be produced beyond C to a point D [P2]. It is to be shown that the exterior angle ACD is greater than each of the interior and opposite angles BAC and ABC.

**Step 2.** Bisect AC at the point E [1.10], so that AE is equal to EC.

**Step 3.** Join BE [P1], and produce BE in a straight line beyond E to a point F [P2]; from the produced line cut off EF equal to BE [1.3]. Join FC [P1].

**Step 4.** In the triangles AEB and CEF, the side AE is equal to the side CE (Step 2), and the side EB is equal to the side EF (Step 3). Moreover, the straight lines AC and BF cut one another at E, so the vertical angles AEB and CEF are equal to one another [1.15].

**Step 5.** Therefore the two sides AE, EB are equal to the two sides CE, EF respectively, and the angles contained by the equal straight lines, namely AEB and CEF, are equal. Hence the base AB is equal to the base CF, the triangle AEB is equal to the triangle CEF, and the remaining angles are equal to the remaining angles, those which the equal sides subtend [1.4]. In particular the angle EAB, subtended by EB, is equal to the angle ECF, subtended by EF; that is, the angle BAC is equal to the angle ECF.

**Step 6.** Since E lies between A and C, and B and F lie on opposite sides of E along the straight line BF, the point F falls on the side of AC remote from B and on the same side of BD as A; thus the straight line CF falls within the angle ECD, and the angle ECF is a part of the angle ECD, which is the same angle as ACD. Therefore the angle ACD is greater than the angle ECF [CN5].

**Step 7.** But the angle ECF is equal to the angle BAC (Step 5). Therefore the angle ACD is greater than the angle BAC.

**Step 8.** Next, produce AC beyond C to a point G [P2]. Bisect BC at the point H [1.10], so that BH is equal to HC. Join AH [P1], produce AH in a straight line beyond H to a point K [P2], cut off HK equal to AH [1.3], and join KC [P1].

**Step 9.** In the triangles AHB and KHC, the side BH is equal to the side CH (Step 8), the side AH is equal to the side KH (Step 8), and the vertical angles AHB and KHC, made by the straight lines BC and AK cutting one another at H, are equal to one another [1.15]. Therefore the two sides BH, HA are equal to the two sides CH, HK respectively, and the contained angles are equal; hence the base AB is equal to the base KC, and the remaining angles are equal to the remaining angles which the equal sides subtend [1.4]. In particular the angle ABH, subtended by HA, is equal to the angle KCH, subtended by HK; that is, the angle ABC is equal to the angle KCB.

**Step 10.** Since H lies between B and C, and A and K lie on opposite sides of H along the straight line AK, the point K falls on the side of BC remote from A and on the same side of AG as B; thus the straight line CK falls within the angle BCG, and the angle KCB is a part of the angle BCG. Therefore the angle BCG is greater than the angle KCB [CN5], and hence the angle BCG is greater than the angle ABC (Step 9).

**Step 11.** But the straight lines AG and BD cut one another at C, so the vertical angles BCG and ACD are equal to one another [1.15]. Therefore the angle ACD is also greater than the angle ABC.

**Step 12.** Hence the exterior angle ACD is greater than each of the interior and opposite angles BAC and ABC. Since the triangle and the side produced were taken arbitrarily, in any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of the interior and opposite angles. Q.E.D.
